entries.target: wine:Bouchard Père & Fils ‘Clos de la Mousse’ Beaune Premier Cru 2022 (375 ml)
entries.value: Bouchard Père & Fils ‘Clos de la Mousse’ Beaune Premier Cru 2022 is Pinot Noir from a small walled vineyard in Beaune that Bouchard has owned alone since 1872, so every bottle is its own. It is aged in the cellars of the Château de Beaune, a fifteenth-century fortress, and the house itself dates from 1731. It tastes of red cherry, raspberry, violet and a little spice, with silky tannin and fresh acidity. It is the half bottle for the Eggs Owen, gentle with short rib braised in red wine and the marchand de vin sauce. We pour it at 58 to 62°F in a Burgundy bowl, never decanted.

entries.target: wine:Ridge Vineyards ‘Estate’ Cabernet Sauvignon Santa Cruz Mountains 2020 (375 ml)
entries.value: Ridge Vineyards ‘Estate’ Cabernet Sauvignon Santa Cruz Mountains 2020 comes from the vineyards around Monte Bello, high on a ridge south of San Francisco, where Ridge was founded in 1962. It is aged in American oak, and Ridge prints every ingredient on the back label. It is structured rather than plush: blackcurrant, cedar, graphite and a savoury herb note, with firm tannin and fresh acidity. Protein and fat soften tannin, so it is the half bottle for the Roasted Chateaubriand and its sauce Foyot. We pour it at 60 to 64°F in a large Bordeaux glass, decanted if the guest likes, or simply swirled.

entries.value: Louis Jadot Meursault 2022 is Chardonnay from Meursault, the Côte de Beaune village known for rich, nutty white Burgundy, aged in barrel for a round, buttery texture. It tastes of ripe lemon, hazelnut and toast, with fresh acidity under the richness. Rich meets rich: it is the half bottle for the Louisiana BBQ Lobster, an extra beside the tasting’s own white, and for the Swordfish Grenobloise and its brown butter. We pour it at 50 to 54°F in a white Burgundy bowl, iced briefly, since too cold hides its richness. Jadot has been a Beaune house since 1859, the head of Bacchus on every label.

entries.target: wine:La Cigarrera Manzanilla Sanlúcar de Barrameda NV (375 ml)
entries.value: La Cigarrera Manzanilla Sanlúcar de Barrameda NV is Palomino from the seaside town at the mouth of the Guadalquivir, where Manzanilla is made. It is aged in a solera under flor, a living layer of yeast that keeps it pale and gives it a salty, bready tang, so it carries no vintage; the cool, humid Atlantic air there keeps the flor thick through the year. It tastes of green apple, chamomile, almond and bread dough, bone dry, fortified but delicate. Our Turtle Soup is finished with aged sherry, so this is its half bottle. We pour 3 oz well chilled, 45 to 48°F, in a white wine glass.

entries.value: Dow’s Vintage Port 2000 comes from Douro grapes of a year the house declared, as it does only in exceptional years. It spends about two years in wood, then ages in bottle, where it throws a crust. It tastes of blackberry, plum, dark chocolate and liquorice, sweet and fortified, its tannin softened by age, with the drier finish Dow’s is known for. A dessert wine should be at least as sweet as the dessert, so it is the half bottle for The Snickers and the Chocolate Crémeux. We stand it upright, then decant it, 3 oz at 60 to 64°F. The Symington family became partners in Dow’s in 1912.
